problem: LLM-based robot task planners are mostly open-loop and lack grounded feedback from physical execution, while conventional RL optimizes sub-symbolic policies that are hard to interpret, and hand-tuned Behavior Trees need heavy manual effort under execution uncertainty.
motivation: Mobile robots face execution uncertainty (layout variation, imperfect localization, control errors), so task-level policies need post-deployment refinement. Scalar rewards cannot separate hardware errors from planning errors, so structured, causal, human-readable feedback is needed for policy updates directly at the symbolic level.
key_idea: Run a closed loop in which a VLM critic watches the physical robot and BT execution traces and writes structured natural-language feedback, and an LLM actor uses that feedback plus the real score to edit an executable Behavior Tree, with no gradients.
insight: Critic domain alignment matters more than model scale: the fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-3B critic gave more stable score gains, accuracy and confidence than the untuned 7B one. Adding symbolic block color info to Gemini gave the most stable convergence, which suggests perception is the bottleneck rather than symbolic planning. The no-critic ablation (score only) barely improves. In a qualitative case the actor treated an unreliable critic as a noisy hypothesis and made conservative BT patches based on trace and score evidence.
method: BT policy representation: task policy is an executable Behavior Tree built from a library of human-designed nodes and subtrees; the initial BT is deliberately simple and encodes no task strategy.

LLM actor: prompted with the task definition, environment spec, node library, BT authoring rules and the current BT; it proposes discrete edits to BT structure and parameters without seeing raw sensor streams. It gets critic feedback F, the real score R and a memory H of past episodes.

VLM critic: sees image snapshots plus BT traces in Initial, Intermediate and Final modes and outputs structured text feedback, an alarm score s in [0,1] (ordinal severity rubric) and a confidence c in [0,1].
Human alarm: a human operator is notified when s>=0.5 or c<0.3.
Episodic VRL loop (Algorithm 1): execute the BT subtree by subtree, critique, update the BT with A(BT,F,R,H), and append {F,R} to actor memory.
Actor observability ablation: optionally give the actor symbolic block color/orientation info (BlockInfo) in addition to critic feedback.
Fine-tuned critic: Qwen2.5-VL-3B fine-tuned on a structured execution-feedback dataset, so critiques map to Impact Issue categories and BT nodes.

setting.backbone: LLM actor (model not stated in the text) + VLM critic: Qwen2.5-VL-7B (frozen), Qwen2.5-VL-3B (fine-tuned), Gemini 3 Pro Preview (frozen)
setting.model_size: 3B / 7B for the Qwen critics; Gemini size not stated
setting.training_data: Only the 3B critic is fine-tuned, on the authors' structured execution-feedback dataset (size not given); the actor and other critics are used off the shelf. The BT is refined over 10 episodes per field configuration.
setting.observation: Image snapshots of the robot and scene for the critic, BT execution traces, and a rule-based real score; the actor gets no raw sensing (optionally symbolic block color/orientation).
setting.action_space: Discrete edits to a Behavior Tree (nodes and parameters); the robot executes BT actions such as navigation between zones, pick, rotate and place
setting.privileged: Rule-based real score per episode is fed to the actor; the BlockInfo variant uses symbolic block color/orientation info; human-annotated severity for the alarm rubric; a human operator is notified on alarms.

numbers_note: Results are given only as figures (mean score, accuracy/IDR, confidence, human alarm curves across episodes); no numeric tables. Table 1 is only the scoring rules.
results: The Gemini 3 Pro + BlockInfo critic gave the highest score growth and most stable convergence, followed by Gemini without BlockInfo, then fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-3B, then untuned Qwen2.5-VL-7B. The no-critic baseline showed extremely slow or no consistent improvement. All findings are qualitative, from curves averaged over 5 field configurations x 10 episodes on a real mobile robot.
limitations: Only qualitative curve-based evidence with no numeric tables, and a single custom task and platform, so generalization is unclear.

The critic works from snapshot windows and cannot detect latent faults with delayed consequences, and the system inherits the critic's perceptual unreliability, which leads to conservative and possibly suboptimal BT patches.
Relies on human-designed node libraries, a rule-based real score and human alarm annotations.
